evals.prompt: I just captured the Archetype Gojira lead preset into the QC. Here are the three takes from one pass: evals/files/qc/DI.wav, evals/files/qc/PLUGIN.wav, evals/files/qc/QC.wav. How close is it?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/analyze.py on the three files, reports LUFS offset, banded deltas, coherence, null depth, interprets against thresholds, and states which claim-ladder rung the capture reached. (The fixture wavs are synthetic — noise DI, band-limited saturated 'plugin', and a low-passed 'QC' — so the numbers are stable across runs; the eval checks the workflow and honesty of interpretation, not real-rig thresholds.)
expectations: scripts/analyze.py is executed on the three wavs
The response reports LUFS offset, per-band deltas, coherence, and null depth as numbers
The verdict names a claim-ladder rung (configured / structurally faithful / measured) and justifies it from the numbers
No number is stated that the script did not produce

evals.prompt: my capture sounds duller than the plugin. should i just redo it or is it actually fine?
evals.expected_output: Asks for (or explains how to record) the one-pass DI/plugin/QC takes rather than guessing; explains which banded delta would confirm 'duller'.
expectations: The response does not declare a verdict without measurement data
It points to the one-cable QC-over-USB recording method as the way to get the takes
It names the high-band spectral delta as the metric that would confirm a dull capture
